PLANET_BONUS.name: Pluto
PLANET_BONUS.note: reclassified as a dwarf planet in 2006

JUPITER_MOON_HINTS.Metis: Orbits closer to Jupiter than any other known moon
JUPITER_MOON_HINTS.Adrastea: The smallest of Jupiter's four inner moons, and the first natural satellite ever discovered in spacecraft images rather than through a telescope
JUPITER_MOON_HINTS.Amalthea: The largest of Jupiter's four inner moons, a reddish potato-shaped body discovered in 1892
JUPITER_MOON_HINTS.Thebe: An inner moon marked by an unusually large crater named Zethus
JUPITER_MOON_HINTS.Io: The most volcanically active body known in the solar system
JUPITER_MOON_HINTS.Europa: An icy moon believed to hide a vast liquid ocean beneath its crust
JUPITER_MOON_HINTS.Ganymede: The largest moon in the solar system, bigger than the planet Mercury
JUPITER_MOON_HINTS.Callisto: The most heavily cratered object known in the solar system
JUPITER_MOON_HINTS.Themisto: An irregular moon orbiting alone between the inner moons and the Himalia group
JUPITER_MOON_HINTS.Leda: The smallest member of the Himalia group of irregular moons, discovered in 1974
JUPITER_MOON_HINTS.Himalia: The largest of Jupiter's irregular moons
JUPITER_MOON_HINTS.Lysithea: The second-smallest member of the Himalia group of irregular moons, discovered in 1938
JUPITER_MOON_HINTS.Elara: An irregular moon named for a mortal woman who bore Zeus's giant son, Tityus
JUPITER_MOON_HINTS.Carpo: A small prograde irregular moon named after a Horae goddess of fruit
JUPITER_MOON_HINTS.Valetudo: A prograde irregular moon, named for a Roman goddess of health, on an orbit that crosses paths with retrograde moons
JUPITER_MOON_HINTS.Ananke: Lends its name to a group of retrograde irregular moons named for a Titaness of necessity
JUPITER_MOON_HINTS.Carme: The largest member of its retrograde irregular moon group, discovered in 1938, holding about 99 percent of that group's total mass
JUPITER_MOON_HINTS.Pasiphae: Lends its name to a group of irregular moons and shares her name with the mythical mother of the Minotaur
JUPITER_MOON_HINTS.Sinope: Discovered in 1914, it was the most distant known moon of Jupiter until the discovery of Megaclite in 2000
JUPITER_MOON_HINTS.Callirrhoe: One of the first irregular moons found by automated sky surveys, discovered in 1999

ELEMENT_HINTS.H: The lightest element and a nonmetal, it is the most abundant element in the universe
ELEMENT_HINTS.He: A noble gas and the second-lightest element, it was first detected in the Sun before being found on Earth
ELEMENT_HINTS.Li: An alkali metal and the lightest solid element, it is widely used in rechargeable batteries
ELEMENT_HINTS.Ne: A noble gas, it produces the familiar bright red-orange glow used in traditional advertising signs
ELEMENT_HINTS.Na: An alkali metal, it reacts violently with water and gives table salt its sodium component
ELEMENT_HINTS.Mg: An alkaline earth metal, it burns with an intense white light and is used in some fireworks and flares
ELEMENT_HINTS.Al: A post-transition metal and the most abundant metal in Earth's crust, it is valued for being lightweight and corrosion-resistant
ELEMENT_HINTS.Si: A metalloid and semiconductor, it is the key material used in most modern computer chips
ELEMENT_HINTS.Cl: A halogen and highly reactive nonmetal, it is widely used to disinfect drinking water
ELEMENT_HINTS.Ar: A noble gas and chemically inert element, it is commonly used to provide an unreactive atmosphere for welding
ELEMENT_HINTS.K: An alkali metal, it is essential to living cells and gives bananas and other foods their potassium content
ELEMENT_HINTS.Fe: A transition metal and the main component of steel, it is also the element that makes blood's hemoglobin able to carry oxygen
ELEMENT_HINTS.Cu: A transition metal, it is one of the best electrical conductors and has given its name to the color copper
ELEMENT_HINTS.Br: A halogen and the only nonmetal that is liquid at room temperature, it is a dark reddish-brown liquid
ELEMENT_HINTS.Kr: A noble gas, its name comes from a Greek word meaning 'hidden'
ELEMENT_HINTS.Ag: A transition metal and the best electrical conductor of any element, it is the shiny metal used in many pieces of jewelry
ELEMENT_HINTS.W: A transition metal with the highest melting point of any element, its symbol comes from the name wolfram
ELEMENT_HINTS.Au: A transition metal and noble metal, it is famously resistant to corrosion and has the chemical symbol Au from its Latin name
ELEMENT_HINTS.Hg: A transition metal and the only metallic element that is liquid at room temperature, it was historically used in thermometers
ELEMENT_HINTS.U: An actinide and naturally radioactive metal, it is the element most associated with the fuel used in nuclear fission reactors
